proposal_reason:
ANALYSIS: No fusion trials yet. Single models reach 0.81-0.83 AUROC, with H-optimus-1 best (0.830). Adding metadata slightly hurts or is neutral, so age/sex carries little signal.
REASONING: Start with the simplest, most robust fusion: early concatenation with balanced blocks, strong regularisation (C=0.01 suits about 5600-d input with 134 patients), no PCA, no L2 norm and meta_weight 1. This gives a reference point for early fusion; later trials will vary C, PCA and late fusion.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.83-0.845, a modest gain over H-optimus-1 alone. If it falls below 0.82, either concatenation dilutes the best model or C is mistuned. I would then test late fusion with mean_prob, and a different C.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion with balanced blocks at C=0.01 reaches 0.824, which is roughly at the level of the best single model (hoptimus1 at 0.830) and not clearly above it. Lepidic and Papillary are the weakest classes (about 0.72-0.73). Late fusion and gated fusion have not been tested yet.
REASONING: In the exploration phase the most informative step is to map the methods. Late fusion with mean_prob is a robust, low-variance ensemble. Each per-model logistic regression keeps its own regularisation, so models with different block sizes cannot dominate one another. A small C (0.01) matches trial #1 for comparability, and l2_normalize=False keeps it close to the baselines.
EXPECTED: I expect an AUROC of about 0.83-0.84, because averaging three comparably strong but different models' probabilities usually helps. If it comes in at or below 0.824, I will conclude that the models' errors are highly correlated and that fusion gains must come from regularisation or preprocessing (L2 norm, PCA) rather than from ensembling.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion (C=0.01, balanced blocks) gets 0.824, roughly equal to the best single model (H-optimus-1 0.830). Late mean_prob reached 0.830, just under the acceptance threshold. Lepidic and Papillary are the weak classes (~0.73). The gated method has not been tested, and neither have C, PCA or L2 normalisation.
REASONING: This is the exploration phase, so I want to map the knobs most likely to matter. Regularisation strength is a key one. With p≈5600 concatenated features against 134 patients, C=0.01 may be too weak or too strong. Testing a much stronger penalty (C=0.001) together with L2 normalisation on early fusion probes both the regularisation and the normalisation axes cheaply. Strong shrinkage often helps mean-pooled foundation-model embeddings in this small-n regime.
EXPECTED: I expect early fusion at about 0.83-0.84 AUROC, which may clear the threshold over #1. If it drops, the optimum is at C≥0.01. In that case I will probe C=0.1 and PCA next, and later test gated and stack late fusion.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion (0.824) and late mean_prob (0.830) are both near the best single model, hoptimus1 at 0.830. L2 norm with lower C gave a small, non-significant gain. Metadata hurts or is neutral in the single-model runs. Fusion so far adds little; Lepidic and Papillary (~0.73) are the weak classes. The gated method is still untested, and so are PCA, meta_weight and stacking.
REASONING: We are still in the exploration phase, so mapping the untested gated method is the most useful step. I chose a heavily regularised configuration to limit overfitting on 134 patients: PCA 64 per model, L2 norm, small hidden size (32), dropout 0.5, weight_decay 0.1, 200 epochs, lr 0.001, 3 seeds. This tests whether per-patient gating over the three models adds anything beyond linear fusion.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC around 0.81-0.83, i.e. roughly on par with early fusion and probably not accepted. If it falls clearly below (<0.80), gated is overfitting or underpowered, and I will drop it in favour of late/early tuning (stack, PCA, C). If it exceeds 0.835, I will refine gated regularisation.

ANALYSIS: All fusion trials sit at about 0.823-0.830, roughly equal to the best single model (H-optimus-1 at 0.830). Late mean_prob and early with L2 norm give small, non-significant gains. Gated fusion matches early fusion but is no better. Metadata hurts or is neutral for single models (meta alone scores 0.60), so meta_weight=1 is already low. Lepidic (~0.74) and Papillary (~0.73) are the weak classes everywhere.
REASONING: Still in exploration, so map the untested knobs that could matter most: PCA and the regularisation strength. Late fusion with mean_prob was the best so far. Late fusion with per-model PCA=64 and L2 norm should reduce noise in each base model, so try it with a higher C=0.1. With 64 dimensions per model, weaker shrinkage is reasonable. mean_logit tends to sharpen agreement between models, which can help AUROC. This trial tests whether dimension reduction combined with weaker regularisation shifts performance beyond the ~0.83 plateau.
EXPECTED: AUROC about 0.83-0.84, which would beat #1 by more than the threshold if PCA denoising helps. If it scores ≤0.825, PCA or the higher C hurts. In that case I would go back to full dimensions with strong shrinkage and explore the combine rules (stack, learned_weights) and the C grid around 0.001-0.01.

ANALYSIS: All fusion variants land at 0.82-0.83, about equal to the best single model (H-optimus-1 0.830). Adding metadata slightly hurts single models. Stronger regularisation (C=0.01, or l2+C=0.001) looks better than PCA64 with C=0.1, which suggests a low-signal, high-dimensional regime. Lepidic and Papillary are the weak classes (~0.73) in every trial.
REASONING: The stack and learned_weights combiners are still untested. Learned weights could upweight H-optimus-1, the strongest single model, while still adding complementary signal from the other two. I keep the trial-2 settings (no L2, no PCA, C=0.01) because they gave the highest AUROC so far, which isolates the combiner as the only change. This maps an open part of the space during exploration.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.83-0.835, possibly clearing the threshold over trial 1. If it is no better than mean_prob, model weighting adds nothing; fusion gains would then have to come from per-model regularisation (smaller C, L2 norm) or a stacker, not from the combiner weights.

ANALYSIS: All fusions cluster at 0.823-0.830 AUROC, roughly the level of the best single model (H-optimus-1 0.8297). Late mean_prob (+0.0058) and early with L2 normalisation (+0.0045) fall just short of their thresholds. PCA-64 with weaker regularisation (C=0.1) hurt, and the gated model matched trial #1 but did not beat it. Adding metadata slightly lowers single-model AUROC, so metadata is not a source of gain.
REASONING: Stacking is the main combiner not yet tested. Per-class AUROCs differ by method (for example, Cribriform is 0.86 under gated versus about 0.81 elsewhere). A stacker on base log-probabilities could learn class-specific trust in each model, which uniform averaging cannot. I keep the base settings that worked best (no L2, no PCA, C=0.01) so only the combiner changes. I use a strongly regularised stacker (stack_C=0.01) because the inner-CV meta-features (21 log-probs plus age/sex) come from only about 134 patients.
EXPECTED: If class-specific weighting helps, AUROC should reach about 0.835 or more, enough to clear the threshold over #1. If it lands at or below 0.83 (or falls because the stacker overfits), I will conclude that combining-rule sophistication is not the bottleneck. I would then spend the remaining exploration on regularisation strength (lower C, L2 normalisation) and PCA in the early method.

ANALYSIS: All fusions sit at 0.824-0.836, barely above the best single model (H-optimus-1, 0.8297). Stacking (#7) gave the highest mean, 0.8358, and a clear Lepidic gain (0.80 vs 0.73-0.75). It still failed the large threshold (0.0208), which points to high per-fold variance of the gain. Simple averaging, learned weights, PCA-64 and the gated network gave no clear gain. Age/sex slightly hurts the single models.
REASONING: Stacking is the only lever that showed a material gain. Its variance probably comes from the second-stage model fitted on about 134 inner-CV predictions. Loosening stack_C to 0.1 tests whether the stacker is under-fitting at 0.01. That would mean it is shrinking toward near-uniform weights while still adding noise. Keeping the base learners fixed (C=0.01, no L2 norm, no PCA) isolates this single knob.
EXPECTED: If stack_C=0.1 lets the stacker use the per-model log-probabilities more fully, AUROC should reach about 0.84 with less fold-to-fold variance, which could clear the threshold. If AUROC drops or the SE grows, the stacker is overfitting at higher capacity. I would then return to stack_C=0.01 or lower and instead vary the base learners (L2 norm with C=0.001, which helped balanced accuracy in #3).

ANALYSIS: All fusions land at 0.817-0.836, near the best single model (H-optimus-1, 0.830). The only clearly higher result is late fusion with stacking at stack_C=0.01 (0.836, with the best Lepidic AUROC of 0.80). It was rejected because its fold-wise gain was noisy (threshold 0.021). Stacking at stack_C=0.1 dropped to 0.816, so the meta-learner overfits as its regularisation weakens. Metadata weight and early-fusion C above 0.01 are still unexplored, but metadata hurt the single models.
REASONING: The trend from stack_C 0.1 to 0.01 suggests stronger shrinkage of the stacker may help further and reduce fold variance. Lower variance is exactly what is needed to pass the corrected-SE threshold. Testing stack_C=0.001 with the same base learners isolates this one knob.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.835-0.84 with lower fold SD, enough for acceptance or close to it. If it falls back toward about 0.826 (the stacker shrunk toward uniform weights), the 0.01 result was a lucky optimum or noise. In that case I would look at base-learner settings instead, such as L2 normalisation with C=0.001 under stacking.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion lands at 0.82-0.836, about the level of the best single model (hoptimus1 0.830). None beats trial #1 by more than the noise threshold. Stacking with stack_C=0.01 gave the highest mean (0.836), but its paired variance is large (threshold 0.021), and neighbouring stack_C values were worse, so that peak is probably noise. Metadata adds little or hurts, and L2 normalisation gave small balanced-accuracy gains in early fusion.
REASONING: The last exploration trial should answer an open question rather than chase the stack peak. Early fusion with PCA per model has not been tested yet. Reducing each block to 32 components cuts 5.6k dimensions to about 96 informative ones, which may let a weaker penalty (C=0.01) fit cross-model signal without overfitting 134 patients. I combine it with L2 normalisation (which helped BA in #3) and balanced blocks.
EXPECTED: If PCA denoising helps, AUROC should reach about 0.835-0.845 with lower fold variance, which could clear the roughly 0.007 threshold against #1. If it lands at or below 0.825, compressing the embeddings does not help. I would then conclude that the fusion ceiling is near the best single model, and spend the remaining budget on a few principled checks (e.g., late fusion with L2 normalisation and mean_prob at a different C) rather than fine-tuning stack_C.

ANALYSIS: All fusion variants cluster at 0.817-0.836, essentially equal to the best single model (H-optimus-1, 0.830). Stacking with stack_C=0.01 gave the highest mean (0.836), but its gain is noisy (threshold 0.021) and its neighbours at 0.1 and 0.001 are lower. Metadata adds nothing and slightly hurts the single models. Late mean_prob at C=0.01 nearly passed (+0.0058 vs a 0.0066 threshold), so low-variance combiners give the most reliable small gains. The base-learner C has not been varied for late fusion, except in #5, which also changed L2 norm and PCA.
REASONING: The cleanest open question is base regularization for late mean_prob. Mean_prob passed the threshold most nearly because its gain variance is low. The C=0.01 setting was inherited from early fusion, where 3x more features call for stronger shrinkage. Per-model logistic regressions on 1.5-2.5k features may prefer weaker shrinkage (C=0.1) without L2 norm or PCA. A clearly better base learner, combined by simple averaging, is the most plausible way to get a gain over trial #1 that the rule accepts.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.83-0.84 with low gain variance, possibly accepted. If AUROC drops below 0.825, C=0.01 is near optimal or stronger shrinkage is needed. In that case the next step is C=0.001 with mean_prob, and I would treat fusion gains as limited by the shared signal across models rather than by the combiner.

ANALYSIS: All fusions land at 0.82–0.836 AUROC, close to the best single model (H-optimus-1, 0.830). Simple late averaging (#2, 0.8298) nearly cleared the low threshold of about 0.0066. Raising C from 0.01 to 0.1 hurt it (#11, 0.8203), and stronger regularisation helped early fusion (#3, C=0.001, 0.8285). Stacking gave the highest mean (#7, 0.8358) but has a large SE, so its threshold is about 0.02 and hard to clear.
REASONING: The clearest trend so far is that stronger regularisation helps. Late mean_prob has the lowest noise threshold of the methods tried, so it is the cheapest place to turn a real gain into an acceptance. This trial changes only C (0.01 to 0.001) from #2, so the dose–response question stays clean.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC around 0.832–0.838, probably with a further gain in Lepidic and Papillary, giving a paired gain of at least 0.007 over #1 and an acceptance. If AUROC falls below #2, then C=0.01 is near the optimum for late fusion. In that case the remaining lever is the combiner (stack with a smaller base C) or meta_weight, not regularisation strength.

ANALYSIS: All fusions sit at 0.82-0.836, close to the best single model (H-optimus-1, 0.830). Only stacking with stack_C=0.01 (#7, 0.8358) gave a sizeable gain. That gain was not accepted because stacking's fold-to-fold variance raises the threshold to about 0.02. Its gain came mostly from Lepidic (0.80 vs 0.73-0.76) and In situ. Per-slide L2 normalisation with stronger shrinkage (#3) was the best early variant. Base-learner C changes under mean_prob had no effect.
REASONING: Keep the most promising combiner (stack, stack_C=0.01) and try to improve its base learners. Use per-slide L2 normalisation with C=0.001, the setting that gave #3 its better balanced accuracy and AUROC among early-fusion runs. Smoother, better-calibrated base log-probabilities should make the stacker's inner-CV inputs less noisy. That could both raise the mean and lower the per-fold variance of the gain, which is what currently blocks acceptance.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.835-0.845, with the Lepidic gain kept and a lower gain SE, enough to clear the threshold. If it lands at or below 0.83, or is again rejected on variance, I will conclude that stacking's apparent edge is mostly noise. I would then test meta_weight and balance_blocks=False in early fusion, or conclude that fusion adds little beyond H-optimus-1.

ANALYSIS: All fusions so far land at 0.816-0.836 AUROC, about the same as the best single model (H-optimus-1, 0.8297). The best raw score is late fusion with stacking (stack_C=0.01, #7), but its fold variance is high, so its acceptance threshold (~0.02) is far above its +0.012 gain. Among early-fusion trials, L2 normalization with strong shrinkage (C=0.001, #3) looked best. PCA, the gated network and other C values gave no signal. Adding age/sex hurts or barely changes single models, so meta_weight is unlikely to matter.
REASONING: One structural knob in early fusion has not been tested: balance_blocks=False. Without block balancing, the models contribute in proportion to their column counts (Virchow2 2560 vs 1536 for each of the others). Under strong L2 shrinkage (C=0.001) this changes how the penalty is shared across models, so the trial is informative. I keep the best early settings from #3 (l2_normalize=True, C=0.001) so that only block balancing changes.
EXPECTED: Most likely the AUROC is similar to or slightly below #3 (~0.82-0.83), because Virchow2 (the weakest model) gets more weight. If it clearly beats #1 by more than the threshold, block balancing was holding fusion back. If not, I will treat early fusion as saturated. I would then move to lower-variance stacking variants (e.g. stack_C=0.01 with base C=0.001 and no L2 normalization) or a heavily regularised gated network.

ANALYSIS: All fusions so far fall in a narrow 0.816–0.836 band, close to the best single model (H-optimus-1, 0.8297). The most promising signal is late mean_prob at C=0.01 (+0.0058, just under its 0.0066 threshold, with a low-variance combiner) and per-slide L2 normalisation in early fusion (0.828). Stacking scores highest but is noisy, with thresholds around 0.021 and sharp sensitivity to stack_C, so it is unlikely to pass. Metadata adds little or even hurts.
REASONING: This trial combines the two ingredients that each nearly passed: the stable, low-threshold late mean_prob combiner and per-slide L2 normalisation with the stronger C=0.001 regularisation that worked in early fusion. Late mean_prob with L2 has not been tested. Its low paired variance against trial #1 gives a realistic chance of clearing a threshold of about 0.006–0.009.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.830–0.835 with balanced accuracy around 0.44–0.45, a gain of about +0.007–0.010 over #1, which may be accepted. If it lands at or below 0.828, the benefit of L2 is method-specific noise, and fusion of linear heads is saturated near the best single model. I would then test meta_weight or a strongly regularised gated configuration before concluding that fusion gives no clear gain.

ANALYSIS: All fusions so far sit at 0.82-0.836 AUROC, statistically tied with the best single model, H-optimus-1 (0.8297). Late stacking with stack_C=0.01 scored highest (0.8358), but its fold variance is high and the acceptance threshold was about 0.02. Linear early and late fusion look saturated across C, L2 normalisation and block balancing. Adding metadata slightly hurts the single models. The one gated trial had a different per-class profile (best Cribriform 0.86 and Papillary 0.75, but weak Lepidic) and lower fold SD.
REASONING: Gated fusion is the least explored method and makes different errors, so it is the most likely place for a clear gain. Trial #4 was moderately regularised. With only 134 patients per fold, a much more constrained version tests whether its weakness was overfitting: smaller PCA (32), hidden=16, dropout 0.5, weight_decay 1.0, and fewer epochs. Raising meta_weight is not worth trying, since metadata adds little.
EXPECTED: If overfitting limited gated fusion, AUROC should rise to about 0.835-0.84, recovering Lepidic while keeping the Cribriform gain, with fold SD below 0.04. If it stays around 0.82-0.83, I will conclude that gating adds nothing beyond linear fusion with this sample size. I would then spend the remaining trials on a few cheap linear checks (early fusion at C=0.0001, stacking with other base C values), accepting that fusion may not clearly beat the best single model.

ANALYSIS: All 16 fusion trials land in 0.816-0.836 AUROC, within noise of the best single model (H-optimus-1, 0.830). Stacking scored highest (0.836 at stack_C=0.01) but has a large threshold (about 0.02) because it is unstable across folds. Early fusion with L2 normalisation and strong shrinkage (C=0.001) is consistently about 0.828 with low fold variance. meta_weight has never been varied; every trial used 1.0.
REASONING: meta_weight is the main untested knob. There is a hint that metadata could matter. The stack, which sees age/sex with less shrinkage, raised Lepidic AUROC to 0.80 from about 0.74 elsewhere. Under the strong L2 shrinkage of C=0.001, age/sex at weight 1 are likely shrunk to near zero. Testing meta_weight=3 on the stable early configuration from #3 (L2 on, C=0.001, balanced blocks) isolates this effect at a low acceptance threshold (about 0.009).
EXPECTED: If metadata helps when less shrunk, AUROC should rise to about 0.835-0.84, mostly through Lepidic and In situ, and the trial could be accepted. If it stays near 0.828 or drops, metadata carries little useful signal, consistent with the single-model +meta baselines not improving. I would then consider meta_weight settled and probe early PCA=128 or C=0.0001 before concluding that fusion is at a plateau.

ANALYSIS: Fusion gains over the accepted best (#1, 0.8240) are consistently small, about +0.004 to +0.006, and below the 0.006-0.009 thresholds. Stacking at stack_C=0.01 had the highest mean (0.836), but its corrected SE is large (threshold about 0.02), so it is unlikely to be accepted. Early fusion with L2 norm and stronger shrinkage (C=0.001) is the most stable improver (about 0.828-0.829 in #3, #14 and #17). Metadata and balance_blocks barely matter.
REASONING: The only monotone signal so far is regularisation strength in early fusion: C=0.01 without L2 gave 0.824, and C=0.001 with L2 gave about 0.828. The next untested step in that direction is C=0.0001 with L2 and balanced blocks. Very strong shrinkage on high-dimensional concatenated features behaves like a nearest-class-mean classifier, which often suits n≈134. That could plausibly give a clearer gain with low fold variance.
EXPECTED: AUROC of about 0.83-0.835, with gains on Acinar, Papillary and Lepidic. If it is at or below 0.828, the shrinkage trend has saturated. I would then conclude that early fusion is capped near the H-optimus-1 single-model level, and switch to a lower-variance late combination, such as stacking with a more regularised base or PCA.

ANALYSIS: All fusion variants fall between 0.816 and 0.836 AUROC, and none clears the paired-SE threshold over #1 (0.824). The best single model, hoptimus1, scores 0.830. Early fusion is flat across L2, balance_blocks and meta_weight, but collapses at C=1e-4. Late stacking at stack_C=0.01 has the highest mean but is too noisy to accept. Gated fusion has only been tried in heavily regularised regimes; it scored about 0.82 but with a different per-class profile (Cribriform 0.84-0.86, higher than other methods).
REASONING: The linear variants look saturated, so further tweaks to them are likely to chase noise. The one clearly open question is whether the gated model is underfitting. Both gated trials used strong regularisation (dropout 0.5, weight decay 0.1-1.0, small hidden). This trial loosens that with a larger hidden size, lower dropout and weight decay, and pca=64 with L2 normalisation, as in #4. Its distinct Cribriform strength suggests a less constrained gate might combine the models complementarily.
EXPECTED: If the gate was underfitting, AUROC should rise to about 0.835-0.84 while Cribriform stays high and Lepidic and Acinar improve. If it stays at or below 0.825, or falls, gated fusion offers no advantage at n=134. I would then conclude the fusion space is essentially flat around 0.825-0.835 and spend the remaining trials on a few late-stack and early-PCA checks before the stop rule ends the search.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion lands at 0.82-0.836, all within noise of trial #1 (0.824) and of the best single model, hoptimus1 (0.830). Stacking with stack_C=0.01 scored highest (0.836), but its paired SE is large (threshold 0.021). Gated fusion is no better or worse. Early fusion is flat across L2/PCA/balance/meta_weight at C=0.001-0.01 (~0.828), and C=0.0001 hurts. Metadata adds little, and sometimes slightly hurts single models.
REASONING: With 6 trials before stop, the one plausible route to a clear gain is stacking, which helped Lepidic and In situ. Its high variance likely comes from noisy base learners and inner-CV predictions. Reducing base-model dimensionality with PCA should make the inner-CV log-probabilities more stable and the stacker less noisy, which lowers the SE. PCA=128 without L2 keeps most of the signal. The other open variable is base C: C=0.01 has been the best base setting, so keep C=0.01 and stack_C=0.01 and change only PCA.
EXPECTED: Expect about 0.835-0.845 AUROC with lower fold variance, which could clear the threshold. If it again lands near 0.83 with a large threshold, I will conclude that fusion gives no reliable gain over the single models on 167 patients. I would then spend the remaining trials on low-risk confirmations rather than tuning.

ANALYSIS: Nothing has beaten #1 (0.824) by more than its noise threshold. Early and mean-prob variants cluster at 0.822-0.829, with gains under the ~0.009 threshold. Stacking with stack_C=0.01 is the clear top signal (0.836 in both #7 and #20, with better Lepidic at 0.80 and Papillary scores), but its fold variance is high, so the threshold is about 0.021. #13 (stack with l2_normalize=True and C=0.001) dropped to 0.816, but it changed two knobs at once, so the cause is unclear.
REASONING: With 5 trials left before the stop rule, the best chance of a clear accepted gain is to refine the stack, which has the largest effect size. This trial isolates l2_normalize under the stack's best settings (C=0.01, stack_C=0.01). Per-slide L2 normalisation raised balanced accuracy in early fusion and may make the base-model log-probabilities more consistent across inner folds. That could lower the stack's fold variance and therefore its acceptance threshold.
EXPECTED: Expect AUROC of about 0.835-0.84 with a lower SE, which could cross the threshold. If it falls to about 0.82 like #13, then L2 normalisation hurts stacking regardless of C. In that case the stack's gain is tied to raw features, and I would try meta_weight or pca variants of #7 instead.

ANALYSIS: No fusion has cleared the noise threshold over #1 (early, 0.8240). Stacking reaches about 0.836, but its paired SE is large (threshold about 0.021), so it cannot be accepted. The near-misses with tight thresholds are late mean_prob at C=0.01 (+0.0058 vs 0.0066) and early L2 at C=0.001 (+0.0045 to +0.0049 vs about 0.009). Gated and PCA variants are neutral or worse, and more or less regularisation of late mean_prob (C=0.1, C=0.001) hurt.
REASONING: Four trials remain before the stop rule. The best use is the variant closest to crossing a low threshold. Late fusion at C=0.01 without L2 or PCA gave the most stable paired gain; only its mean_prob combiner has been tested there. mean_logit (geometric mean) was tried only with PCA 64 and C=0.1, both of which were separately harmful. Under a geometric mean, a model that confidently rejects a class pulls that class down. This could sharpen the ranking for the weak classes (Lepidic, Papillary) while keeping fold variance low like mean_prob. That makes it a plausible way to gain the needed ~0.001-0.003 at a threshold near 0.006.
EXPECTED: AUROC about 0.830-0.833 with fold SD near 0.044, and a paired gain over #1 just above a threshold of about 0.006, which would be accepted. If it lands at or below mean_prob (about 0.830, rejected), I conclude that combiner choice among simple averages is noise. Late fusion would then sit at about the H-optimus-1 single-model level, and the remaining budget should go to early L2 at C=0.001 with higher meta_weight, or I should accept that fusion gives no reliable gain here.

ANALYSIS: Fusion gains are small. Late mean_logit (#22, 0.8307) is accepted, and stacking reaches about 0.836 but cannot clear its high, variance-inflated threshold of about 0.02. C=0.01 is consistently the best base regularisation. L2 normalisation, PCA=128, meta_weight and balance_blocks have each moved AUROC by less than 0.005. Gated fusion overfits.
REASONING: The best combiner has only been tested on raw features. PCA=64 was tried for late fusion only together with L2 and C=0.1 (#5), so its effect is confounded. Applying PCA=64 alone to the accepted config isolates whether compressing each model's representation helps the per-model logistic regressions. With 134 training patients and 1.5k to 2.5k dimensions, a lower-variance basis could plausibly sharpen the weak classes (Lepidic, Papillary).
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC between 0.825 and 0.840. If it is not accepted (gain below about 0.005), I will conclude that representation compression is not a lever. In that case, remaining effort should go to the combiner and base C around mean_logit, or to accepting that fusion is near its ceiling of about 0.83.

ANALYSIS: Late fusion with C=0.01, no L2 and no PCA is the best region so far. Mean_logit (#22, 0.8307) was accepted. Stacking reaches the highest raw means (about 0.836), but its fold-to-fold variance is high, so its thresholds sit around 0.02 and its balanced accuracy drops. C is clearly optimal at 0.01, and L2 and PCA change little. Metadata weighting has only been probed in early fusion, where meta_weight=3 gave a negligible gain.
REASONING: The main untested axis in the winning late mean_logit setup is how much each base model relies on age/sex. Age may carry signal for In situ and Lepidic, the most indolent patterns, and Lepidic is a weak class at about 0.75. Setting meta_weight=3 in late mean_logit tests this cheaply on the best configuration, without the variance penalty of stacking. The other untried options look worse: further C, PCA or L2 tweaks have shown near-zero effects, and weighted_vote produces coarse scores that should hurt AUROC.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.830–0.836, with a possible gain on Lepidic and In situ. If it is neutral or worse, metadata upweighting is not useful. I would then consider the late mean_logit plateau reached and spend the remaining trials on lower-variance stacking variants, or stop exploring small knobs.

ANALYSIS: Fusion gives only small, consistent gains over the best single model (H-optimus-1 0.8297). Late mean_logit (C=0.01, raw features) is accepted at 0.8307. Stacking reaches about 0.836 but its fold variance is high, so its acceptance threshold is around 0.02 and it never passes. Gated nets and strong PCA do not help. Metadata weight has little effect, and C=0.01 is the sweet spot for late fusion.
REASONING: One open question is whether per-slide L2 normalisation helps late fusion at the best C. Trial #15 tested L2 only at C=0.001 with mean_prob, and #21 only with stack. For early fusion, L2 improved BA, and it may make base learners steadier across folds. That would tighten the paired SE and could also lift AUROC.
EXPECTED: Expect AUROC around 0.830–0.835. A gain above about 0.005 would be accepted. If it lands at or below 0.83, conclude L2 does not help late fusion, and that fusion has plateaued near 0.83. The remaining budget should then test a few untried, structurally different options rather than re-tuning near the best.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion family lands at about 0.82-0.836 AUROC, essentially tied with the best single model (H-optimus-1, 0.8297). Late mean_logit at C=0.01 (#22) is the only accepted gain, and only marginally. Stacking gives the highest means (~0.836), but its paired variance is large (threshold ~0.021), so it cannot be accepted. Neither L2 norm, PCA, meta_weight nor gating has moved the score beyond noise, and the gated model degrades as its capacity grows.
REASONING: The main untested combiner is weighted_vote, which is the last unmapped region of late fusion. Trying it closes the open question about combiners at the known-best base settings (C=0.01, no L2, no PCA, meta_weight=1). It costs one trial and should be checked before declaring a plateau. Further fine-tuning of continuous knobs around #22 would only chase gains below the ~0.005 threshold.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC at or below #22, about 0.82-0.83, because hard or weighted votes give coarser scores, which tends to hurt ranking-based AUROC. If it is clearly better (gain above the ~0.005 threshold), confidence-weighted agreement between models carries signal and the voting variants deserve follow-up. If not, the combiner space is exhausted and the search can stop on #22.

ANALYSIS: Most fusions sit at an AUROC of about 0.82–0.83, roughly level with the best single model (H-optimus-1, 0.8297). Late mean_logit (#22, 0.8307) was accepted on low fold variance. Stacking with stack_C=0.01 gives the highest means (#7 0.8358, #20 0.8356 with PCA 128), helped mainly by Lepidic (0.80 vs 0.75). Its paired variance is high, though, so the threshold is about 0.02. Gated runs, very small C and L2-normalised stacks are all worse.
REASONING: Stacking is the only lever with a clearly higher mean, so the open question is whether its fold-to-fold noise can be cut. Stronger compression of the base models (PCA 64, vs 128 or none) could make the inner-CV base log-probabilities more stable. That would lower the variance of the paired gain and could bring stacking's ~+0.005 to +0.01 advantage close to the threshold. All other knobs stay at the best-known stack setting so the PCA effect is isolated.
EXPECTED: Expected AUROC about 0.835, with Lepidic and Papillary holding their stacking gains and a smaller paired SE than #7/#20. If it is again rejected with a threshold near 0.02, or the mean falls below 0.833, stacking's gain is not separable from noise on 134 patients. I would then stop pursuing stacking and treat late mean_logit as effectively optimal, spending the remaining trials only on clearly distinct questions.

ANALYSIS: Current best is late mean_logit with C=0.01, raw features, and AUROC 0.8307. That is only marginally above the best single model, H-optimus-1 at 0.8297. Stacking with stack_C=0.01 gives the highest means (0.834-0.836), but its fold variance is large, so the acceptance thresholds are about 0.02 and stacking never clears them. Variations to early fusion, gated fusion and the meta weight have all landed within noise. C=0.01 looks near-optimal for late fusion, and C=0.001 has worked best for early fusion with L2 normalisation.
REASONING: One untested combination could plausibly give a clear gain: mean_logit late fusion with PCA 128, which is milder than PCA 64. A stronger alternative is mean_logit with C=0.001 and no L2 normalisation, which is also untested; for mean_prob, C=0.001 lost slightly. Most remaining small tweaks will probably sit below the roughly 0.005 threshold. I prefer testing mean_logit at C=0.001, because stronger shrinkage of each base model before taking the geometric mean may calibrate logits better and lift the small classes (Cribriform rose to 0.83 under mean_prob at C=0.001). This also completes the C sweep for the accepted method.
EXPECTED: AUROC about 0.828-0.835. If it does not beat 0.8307 by more than the threshold, I will conclude that late fusion is saturated with respect to C. I would then spend the remaining budget on a few stacking variants (for example pca=32 with stack_C=0.01) before accepting #22 as final.

ANALYSIS: Fusion has plateaued around 0.828-0.836. Late mean_logit at C=0.01 without L2 or PCA (#22, 0.8307) is the accepted best. Stacking reaches about 0.835, but its paired SE is large (threshold about 0.021), so it cannot be accepted. C=0.01 is clearly the best regularisation for late fusion, while early fusion does best near C=0.001 with L2 (0.828-0.829). Gated fusion is consistently worse, and meta_weight and PCA have only noise-level effects.
REASONING: One cell of the early-fusion grid is still open: no per-slide L2 at C=0.001. #1 used no L2 with C=0.01, and all the C=0.001 runs used L2. L2 slightly hurt late fusion (#25 vs #22), so dropping it at the regularisation strength that suits early fusion could give a lift. Early fusion can also learn cross-model interactions that late fusion cannot. This is the main untested, plausible direction left; the others are tiny knob tweaks.
EXPECTED: Expect AUROC around 0.83-0.84 with better balanced accuracy (about 0.45). If it stays at or below about 0.832 (not accepted), then early and late linear fusion are equivalent here. In that case the remaining budget should go only to a few variance-reducing checks, such as late mean_logit with pca=128, before the search stops at the plateau.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion method has plateaued near 0.825-0.836 AUROC. The current best is late mean_logit (C=0.01, no L2, no PCA) at 0.8307, which edges past hoptimus1 alone (0.8297). Stacking has the highest means (about 0.836, driven by Lepidic at 0.80), but its fold variance gives an acceptance threshold near 0.02, so it cannot be accepted. Gated networks underperform, and L2 normalisation or meta_weight changes give no gain.
REASONING: One region is still unmapped: early fusion with per-model PCA and no L2 at moderate C. Early fusion with L2 and PCA=32 (#10) was weaker. Without PCA, early fusion needed C=0.001 to reach about 0.829. PCA=64 per model (192 features in total) with C=0.01 could keep the denoising seen with late PCA=64 (#23, the best late mean) while letting the joint classifier use cross-model interactions with less shrinkage. This tests whether the early-fusion ceiling is set by dimensionality rather than by the fusion type.
EXPECTED: If dimensionality is the limit, I expect about 0.833-0.840 with a lower fold SD than stacking, which could clear the roughly 0.005 threshold. If it comes back at 0.83 or below, early fusion is capped like the other methods. I would then conclude the 0.83 plateau reflects shared information across the foundation models, not a fusion choice, and spend the remaining trials only on low-variance late variants.

ANALYSIS: The accepted best, late mean_logit at C=0.01 with raw features (0.8307), is about 0.001 above the best single model, H-optimus-1 (0.8297), so fusion has not yet clearly beaten the baselines. Stacking at stack_C=0.01 consistently gives the highest means (0.834-0.836), mainly through Lepidic (0.80 vs 0.75). Its fold variance is high, though, so its acceptance threshold is about 0.02 and it has never been accepted. Early fusion plateaus near 0.829, gated fusion is worse, and C=0.01 is the best base strength.
REASONING: One untested lever is a less regularised base model (C=0.1) feeding the stacker at stack_C=0.01. Stronger base probabilities could give the stacker more contrast to exploit, and C=0.1 has only been tried with mean_prob and with PCA plus mean_logit. Weaker, already-tested alternatives are mean_logit with PCA=128 or meta_weight=10. Stacking is the only family showing a meaningfully larger mean, so this probes its main remaining knob, the base C. Keeping PCA off avoids duplicating #20 and #27.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.835-0.84 if the sharper base outputs help the stacker, though passing the roughly 0.02 threshold is unlikely. If it falls below about 0.83, I will conclude stacking is capped by inner-CV noise. In that case I would spend the remaining budget on low-variance late or early variants, such as mean_logit with PCA=128 or a higher meta_weight, and accept that fusion gives at most a marginal gain over H-optimus-1.

ANALYSIS: Fusion has plateaued at about 0.825-0.836 AUROC. Only late mean_logit (#22, 0.8307) was accepted, and it beats the best single model (H-optimus-1, 0.8297) by a negligible margin. Stacking with stack_C=0.01 scores highest (0.834-0.836) and lifts Lepidic from 0.75 to 0.80. However, its fold variance gives a threshold of about 0.02, so it is never accepted. Gated is consistently worse. L2 norm, PCA, meta_weight and balance_blocks all shift scores by less than the noise.
REASONING: The most promising open lead is to make stacking less variable while keeping its Lepidic gain. Stacking has been tested with unnormalised base models only at C=0.01 and 0.1. At C=0.001 it was tried only with L2 norm (#13, worse). Unnormalised base models at C=0.001 gave the best balanced accuracy in other methods (#12 mean_prob, #28 mean_logit, #29 early). Smoother, better-calibrated base log-probabilities may make the inner-CV meta-features more stable, which would lower the per-fold variance of the gain and therefore the threshold.
EXPECTED: Expected AUROC is about 0.833-0.840, with Lepidic held near 0.80 and a fold SD at or below 0.039. If it is again rejected with a gain of about 0.005-0.01 against a threshold of about 0.02, I conclude that stacking's advantage is not resolvable at n=167. I would then spend the remaining trials on a couple of final checks before letting the stop rule end the search, and report #22 as essentially tied with H-optimus-1.

ANALYSIS: Late fusion with combine=mean_logit and C=0.01 (#22, 0.8307) is the only accepted fusion, and only by a small margin. Stacking reaches the highest raw means (0.835–0.836) but has very noisy per-fold gains, so its acceptance threshold is about 0.02 and it cannot be accepted. Early fusion, gated fusion, L2 normalisation, meta_weight and other C values all fall within ±0.005 of the best or below it. The space looks largely saturated around 0.83 AUROC.
REASONING: Adding PCA to the best mean_logit recipe was the only near-best variation with a positive trend (#23, pca=64: +0.0016, against a low threshold of about 0.005). That threshold is low because mean_logit gains are stable across folds. pca=128 keeps more signal than 64 while still removing noisy directions. It is the last untested low-variance tweak with a plausible clear gain, and it checks whether the PCA trend is real or noise.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.832–0.836, with Lepidic and Acinar improving slightly. If the gain stays under the threshold of about 0.005, I will conclude that dimensionality reduction does not help late fusion. #22 would then remain the final configuration, and the few remaining trials should go to structurally different ideas rather than small knob changes.

ANALYSIS: Fusion plateaus at about 0.83 AUROC. Late mean_logit (C=0.01, raw features) is the accepted best at 0.8307. Stacking reaches about 0.836 but its paired gains are noisy (threshold about 0.02), so it is never accepted. Early fusion, gated fusion, l2 normalisation, meta_weight=3 and C away from 0.01 all fail to help. PCA 64 and 128 on mean_logit gave only tiny positive gains (+0.0016, +0.0004).
REASONING: Four trials remain before the stop rule. The one remaining cheap axis with a consistent small positive sign is per-model PCA under mean_logit. Stronger compression (32) could reduce the variance of each base model enough to give a clearer gain, especially on the weak Lepidic and Papillary classes. Stack is too noisy to pass the threshold, and gated is consistently worse.
EXPECTED: Expect about 0.832-0.836 with low paired variance, possibly passing the roughly 0.005 threshold. If it is flat or worse, PCA does not help. I would then conclude the fusion ceiling is about 0.83 and accept #22 as final.

ANALYSIS: Fusion gains are small. Late mean_logit (#22, 0.8307) was accepted, but only by a hair. Stacking reaches about 0.835 repeatedly, yet its per-fold gains are noisy, which pushes the acceptance threshold to about 0.02. C=0.01 without PCA or L2 is consistently the best regime. Gated runs have all trailed (0.80–0.823), and the more capacity they had, the worse they did.
REASONING: Only 3 trials remain before the stop rule. More stack and PCA variants have repeatedly landed inside the noise band, so another one is unlikely to clear a threshold of about 0.02. One open question about the space remains: every gated run used l2_normalize=True, while the linear methods did as well or better without L2. A gated run with low capacity, no L2, PCA=32, strong dropout, moderate weight decay and a short schedule tests whether a patient-level gate can add complementary signal once regularised to linear-like capacity. This is the one remaining direction with a plausible chance of a non-incremental gain.
EXPECTED: Most likely AUROC is around 0.82–0.83, not accepted. Lepidic and Papillary, the weak classes, would need to rise for it to pass. If it fails, I will conclude that gating adds no value at n=134 and that the fusion ceiling is about 0.83. Then #22 (late mean_logit) stands as the final, robust choice, and stack's higher mean is not distinguishable from noise.

ANALYSIS: Linear fusions sit around 0.825-0.836 AUROC, only marginally above H-optimus-1 alone (0.830). Late mean_logit (#22, 0.8307) is the only accepted gain. Stacking with stack_C=0.01 has the highest means (0.834-0.836) and lifts Lepidic from 0.75 to 0.80, but its fold variance makes the threshold about 0.021, so none of those gains were accepted. Gated models and very strong or very weak regularisation are consistently worse.
REASONING: Two trials remain before the stop rule. The only family with a mean gain near the threshold is stacking (C=0.01, stack_C=0.01), so a new trial should try to shift that mean further. Raising meta_weight to 3 reduces shrinkage of age/sex in the base models. That might sharpen the Lepidic and In situ separation the stacker exploits, a pattern that could correlate with age. This is a stacking variant not yet tried and not a re-run of noise-level knobs.
EXPECTED: Expected AUROC is about 0.833-0.840, a gain of +0.005 to +0.01 over #22. That is probably still below the ~0.02 stacking threshold, so acceptance is unlikely. If it fails, the conclusion is that fusion offers at most about a 0.005 AUROC benefit over the best single model on 167 patients. Late mean_logit (#22) should then be kept as the final, low-variance choice rather than chasing stacking noise.

ANALYSIS: Fusion has plateaued at about 0.83 AUROC. Late mean_logit (#22, 0.8307) is the only accepted fusion, and it barely beats the best single model, hoptimus1 at 0.8297. Stacking with stack_C=0.01 is consistently highest (0.834–0.836 across pca None/128/64 and meta 1/3), with Lepidic rising to 0.80. Its fold-to-fold variance pushes the threshold to about 0.02, so its gains of about +0.012 are not accepted. Gated and early fusion, PCA, L2 normalisation and meta_weight changes give nothing beyond noise.
REASONING: This is the last trial before the stop rule fires, so it should target the only lever with a consistent positive signal: the stacker. Stacking at pca=128/64/None gave the same score, and with no PCA it was best at C=0.01 (C=0.001 and 0.1 were worse). Untested is stronger compression to pca=32 at the same C=0.01 and stack_C=0.01. This could make the base models' inner-CV log-probabilities smoother and better calibrated. That would cut the stacker's per-fold variance, the thing that currently blocks acceptance, while keeping the Lepidic and Papillary gains.
EXPECTED: Mean AUROC of about 0.833–0.838, ideally with a lower fold SD and higher paired correlation with #22, so the threshold shrinks toward 0.01. If it is rejected, stacking's apparent +0.01 edge is too unstable to verify at n=167. In that case I conclude that simple late mean_logit fusion (#22) is the defensible final choice and that fusion gives at most a marginal gain over H-optimus-1 alone.
